question.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$

current_example.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.35$ | $0.05$ |

Calculate $\textrm E[X^2].$
current_example.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^2$ is given by

$$
\textrm E[X^2] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^2 \cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={0}^{2}\cdot 0.2+{1}^{2}\cdot 0.25+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.15+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.35+{4}^{2}\cdot 0.05 \\  & =0\cdot 0.2+1\cdot 0.25+4\cdot 0.15+9\cdot 0.35+16\cdot 0.05 \\  & =4.8.\end{aligned}
$$
